Bayesian design-comparable between-case standardized mean difference

Source: R/utils-bayes-meta.R
bc_smd_bayes.Rd

Fits one study's multiple-baseline (multiple-probe) or treatment-reversal data with a Gaussian piecewise multilevel model in brms and returns the posterior of the design-comparable BC-SMD, computed draw by draw as \(\delta_{AB} = p'\beta / \sqrt{r'\theta}\).

Usage

bc_smd_bayes(
  data,
  design = detect_design_type(data),
  time_A = NULL,
  time_B = NULL,
  trend = c("none", "fixed", "random"),
  ar = TRUE,
  family = "gaussian",
  priors = NULL,
  iter = 2000,
  chains = 4,
  outcome_var = "outcome",
  intervention_goal = c("increase", "decrease"),
  ab_rule = c("scdhlm", "shortest_treatment"),
  duration = NULL,
  random_effect = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

data

One study's data with case, phase, time and outcome columns.

design

"multiple_baseline", "multiple_probe", or "reversal"; defaults to detect_design_type().

time_A, time_B

Sessions \(A\) and \(B\); NULL uses the defaults in Details.

trend

"none", "fixed", or "random" time trend.

ar

Logical; AR(1) residuals within series.

family

Must be "gaussian".

priors

brms priors; NULL uses the package defaults scaled to the outcome SD plus the bounded AR(1) prior.

iter, chains

Sampler settings.

outcome_var

Outcome column.

intervention_goal

"increase" or "decrease"; with "decrease" the sign of \(\delta_{AB}\) is reversed.

ab_rule

"scdhlm" or "shortest_treatment"; the default rule for \(B\) (see Details).

duration

Optional \(B - A\) in sessions; overrides ab_rule.

random_effect

Logical; let the treatment effect vary across cases (default TRUE). FALSE fits a common-effect model, useful as a sensitivity check.

...

Passed to brms::brm().

Value

A list with summary (one-row data frame: estimate (posterior median), sd, lower, upper (95\ credible bounds)), draws (numeric vector of \(\delta_{AB}\) draws), n_nonfinite, time_A, time_B, n_cases (participants), n_series, design, and model (the brmsfit).

Details

Effect size. \(\delta_{AB}\) is the model-implied difference between the average outcome at follow-up session \(B\) when treatment is introduced just after session \(A\) and the average outcome at \(B\) without treatment, divided by the standard deviation of the outcome at \(B\) without treatment. With intervention_goal = "decrease" the draws are multiplied by \(-1\), so a positive \(\delta_{AB}\) always means improvement, the orientation meta_bayes() expects.

Model. Rows with a baseline-role or intervention-role phase are kept (maintenance and generalization rows are dropped); the tiers of tier_vars() are the series. For multiple-baseline data the fixed part uses the package's AB coding (see process_scd_phases()): level_AB for trend = "none", plus time_A and trend_AB for "fixed" and a series-varying time_A for "random"; time_A counts sessions from the earliest session across all series, one origin as in scdhlm. Series carry a random intercept, and by default (random_effect = TRUE) the treatment effect varies too, (1 + level_AB | case), matching the one-stage default; this leaves the form of \(\delta_{AB}\) unchanged. For reversal data a single treatment indicator (intervention role vs baseline role) is the effect; "fixed" and "random" add only the baseline time trend time_A. With ar = TRUE the residuals follow a stationary AR(1) process within series with a uniform(-1, 1) prior bounded to \([-1, 1]\).

Participants and series. When a participant carries several series (a replicated multiple baseline across behaviors or settings) the model adds a participant level, outer, above the series; in a clustered multiple baseline (a cluster column with two or more clusters) outer is the cluster. The outer level carries an intercept and, with random_effect = TRUE, a varying treatment effect, (1 + level_AB | outer) ((1 + treatment | outer) for reversal data); random_effect = FALSE keeps (1 | outer). Both intercept variances enter \(r'\theta\). Data with both a cluster column and several series per participant stop. At least three participants are required; series of one participant do not count separately.

Numerator \(p'\beta\). The level_AB (or treatment) coefficient plus, for multiple-baseline models with a trend, the trend_AB coefficient times \(B - T_B\), where \(T_B\) is the first observed session after \(A\), matching the coding of trend_AB.

Denominator \(r'\theta\). Per draw, the untreated between-series variance at \(B\), \(\tau_0^2 + 2\tau_{02}(B - T_A) + \tau_2^2 (B - T_A)^2\) (the last two terms only with random trends; \(T_A\) is the earliest first baseline session), the participant or cluster intercept variance when present, and the within-series variance. brms parameterizes AR(1) residuals by the innovation SD sigma, so the stationary residual variance is \(\sigma^2 / (1 - \phi^2)\), the level-1 variance.

Times. \(A\) is the last session of the shortest baseline across series. ab_rule = "shortest_treatment" sets \(B\) from the shortest treatment duration across cases; scdhlm::default_times() instead adds to \(A\) the treatment duration of the case(s) with that shortest baseline. With ab_rule = "scdhlm" (default) \(B\) follows scdhlm, so a comparison with its REML estimate is like for like. duration sets \(B - A\) directly, for a common benchmark duration across the studies of a meta-analysis; time_B overrides both. For reversal data both times refer to the first baseline phase and the first treatment phase: \(B\) never passes the end of the first treatment phase. With trend = "none" and no random trend, \(\delta_{AB}\) does not depend on \(A\) or \(B\).

Uncertainty. The REML estimator applies a small-sample correction \(J\); here the posterior of \(\delta_{AB}\) carries the uncertainty in every parameter, so no \(J\) correction is applied. Draws that are not finite (for example from \(|\phi| = 1\)) are dropped from the summary and counted in n_nonfinite.

The BC-SMD rests on Gaussian errors, so only family = "gaussian" is accepted; count or proportion outcomes go through the one-stage GLMM path (run_scd_analysis(), marginal_contrast()). scdbayes does not compute the within-case SMD, which is biased under autocorrelation.

Examples

if (interactive()) {
  d <- simulate_scd_data(n_cases = 4)
  bc_smd_bayes(d, design = "multiple_baseline", trend = "fixed")$summary
}
